turns.t: Er, hi. I've got a lump on my neck, at the back, and it's gone sore. It's a cyst, I think. I've had them before.
Let me hear about it. How long has it been there?
Ages. A year? It was small and didn't bother me. Then last week it got big and sore.
Painful how?
Tender. Throbs a bit. It hurts if my collar rubs it.
Any discharge, or has it burst?
No. Nothing came out. No.
What are you using on it?
Doxycycline, 100 mg, the dentist gave me some, maybe once a day? And the antiseptic wash, I don't know the name, from the pharmacy.
Thanks. So doxycycline, 100 mg, once a day as you recall it. And the wash, you can't name it. Have you had cysts before?
One on my back, they cut it out, five years ago.
Does it run in the family?
My dad gets them. On his scalp.
Let me look. Which side? ~
Back of the neck, a bit to the right.
It's a round, firm lump about two centimetres across, tender, with a tiny dark dot in the middle. The skin around is slightly red. ~
Is that a cyst, then? ~
It looks like an epidermoid cyst, which is a sac under the skin, and it's a little inflamed.
Will it go away? ~
Inflamed ones often settle for a while, but the sac stays, and it usually flares again. Taking the whole sac out is the proper cure. ~
Operation? ~
A small one, under local anaesthetic. First, I'd like to arrange an ultrasound, to check the size and make sure it's what I think.
Okay. ~
Keep the area clean, don't squeeze it, and put a warm flannel on it for ten minutes a few times a day.
Squeeze is what I want to do. ~
I know, but squeezing pushes the contents deeper and can cause an infection. ~
Right. ~
If it turns very red and hot, gets much more painful, starts to ooze pus, or you get a fever, come back that day.
I will. Thanks. ~
And if the ultrasound confirms it, we'll talk about getting it removed once it's calm. ~
